review:
So I was deciding whether to do a serious review on Goat Simulator because I haven't seen one on Steam; so rather than join the bandwagon of unfunny jokey reviews for the game, I'll stick to my guns...

Goat Simulator does exactly what it says on the tin; you play as a Goat, You cause havoc wherever you go; trashing, bashing, causing explosions, destroying houses, jumping on trampolines, basically anything you want. With plenty of interactive objects in the game, you can spend plenty of time wandering around never finding a dull moment. 

The graphics in goat simulator are really nice. They aren't on the levels of Evolve or something, but for this type of game, you aren't really going to be playing for the top of the range graphics.  The music and audio are exactly what you would expect here; derpy music in the background as you potter about the city, along with cries of fear from the civilians as the demon goat runs rampant.

There are three different areas in Goat Simulator; each zone is huge, ranging from theme parks, to crop fields, every building has something to do in it, every room has something to interact with or destroy. I honestly don't think there is anything wrong with either of the levels included here.  There is nothing difficult in the game to do here at all. There are no real objectives, just an open world sandbox game where you do whatever you want, whenever you want. 

I have managed to put about twenty hours into Goat Simulator; most of this time was playing on local screen co-op with my girlfriend, and then a couple more hours’ achievement hunting, and boy there is some pretty ridiculous achievements to do. Other than the developers openly coming out stating that they would not be fixing any bugs in the game, I had no real game breaking bugs, apart from sometimes falling through the world; however this was fixed easily by just respawning again. 

If you want a game that is just purely for messing around in with no real aim and wanting some real stupidity, then Goat Simulator will give you plenty of fun; granted this type of game is not for everyone, I enjoyed it though.

If you are unfamiliar with Goat Simulator - it was developed in a few weeks and became an internet phenomenon somewhat due to embracing its absurdity with buggy controls and a twitchy camera. The game's graphics have rough edges, but its robust engine fosters experimentation and creativity. Lacking a deep narrative, Goat Simulator thrives on rather standard sandbox features, where quests act as tutorials, but real joy comes from chaotic experimentation and the hunt for Easter eggs and the achievements tied to them. Whether it's running through houses, destroying property, upending a BBQ party, or licking unsuspecting pedestrians to induce comical panic, Goat Simulator thrives on the player's desire to push the boundaries of absurdity. Even attempting to end the goat's life through extreme measures, like head-butting a gas station, results in unexpected achievements, showcasing the game's commitment to rewarding creativity. Ever seen a goat fly? Well here's your chance.

Something I had missed the first time I played Goat Simulator (back around 2017) was the Steam Workshop integration and its community. As you would expect, this greatly helps extend the life of the games and help pump content into it that would otherwise not exist. It goes a long way and now almost 10 years after its release, there is an absolute ton of community content to play around with in addition to the free official content that has since been added.

For those seeking an escape from the ordinary, Goat Simulator beckons with its ridiculous ride, challenging players to embrace the unconventional and revel in the sheer joy of being a goat on a mission to cause chaos. It's rare you'll find another game this silly and this fun. Sir Whoopass is the closest that comes to mind.

I definitely recommend Goat Simulator.

I'll spare you the joke review, and give you some info into wether you should actually buy Goat Simulator. Though, since the extremely silly nature of the game, joke reviews are probably fitting since you really have to be aligned with this games' sense of humor to get the most out of it.

The hilarity of the game already escaped me prior to play because I already understood what the game's comedy is all out about in a single first impression/Let's play video - if you're still laughing throughout an entire video of Goat Simulator being played, then playing it should be a no brainer for you. If your first response is something like "Oh, i get it. Absurd physics, and semi-glitchiness mixed with platforming, level exploration, destruction and Tony Hawk Pro Skater style scoring system" and you aren't too amused, you can probably pass on Goat Simulator. I decided to bother because THPS scoring and level exploration appealed to me, but that soon wore off once I found the only reason to get score was to complete quests (or get on leaderboards). While doing insane combo strings in THPS is fun because of responsive controls, good level design, and time based challenge, Goat Simulator to me is less fun since you have to wrestle with wonky physics that will put get you stuck under objects or inside the level geometry, loosing your combo.

Despite my negativity, I do find Goat Simulator amusing and I kinda like exploring the different part of level to see what non-sense the developers created, or to see how I can string together licking objects, headbutting people, jumping and tricking over things (front/backflips and/or spins), or blowing things up to see what kind of combos I can get. The quests aren't very well explained though, so if you can't quite figure them out from their vague descriptions, then you'd have to rely on a guide - if you're still willing to put up with completing the levels in the game. Goat Simulator is near exclusively a "goof off" game or something you play on TWitch/Youtube, or to show to friends for its absurdity. I don't know what happens when you "complete" a level, but I never felt like I was obtaining a goal by trying to. 

Coffee Stain Studio also deserves props for giving away the MMO expansion for free, and creating a surprisingly convincing simulation of an MMORPG experience - as the store page says, It felt like it was a real MMO, with real players moving, fighting and chatting. The GoatZ addon seems to have a decent amount of content and different "survival game like gameplay", but by that point, I've already lost interest, especially since my goat got glitched nside a wall and I wasn't able to respawn like yoiu could in the other modes/levels.

Goat Simulator didn't hold my attention once I figured out the breadth of the gameplay, and I lost interest fairly quickly. That said, the game does exactly as it intended and there is some amusing content here. I'm giving Goat Simulator a positive recommendation if you are seeking a non-sensical, Tony Hawk style, physics based platforming sandbox, for some reason, (say if you like score attack games or questing/platforming). If the humor does little to nothing for you, than the gameplay likely won't either.
Playing this game is like making love to a beautiful woman. It’s something I can only do when I’m a goat.

[h1] Goat Simulator – A Masterpiece of Sheer Chaos and Bleating Brilliance [/h1]  

Ah yes, [b]Goat Simulator[/b], the game that boldly asks, "[i]What if a goat could headbutt reality itself?[/i]" If you've ever woken up and thought, "[i]I want to wreak havoc as a physics-defying goat,[/i]" then congratulations – your oddly specific dream is now a reality.  

This is not just a game; it's a [b]life experience[/b]. Forget saving kingdoms, fighting dragons, or becoming a space marine – you're a goat, and your only mission is to turn everything into absolute chaos. Climb ladders with your nonexistent hands, lick random objects (because goats apparently have magnetic tongues), and launch yourself into orbit because physics in this universe took a permanent vacation.  

[hr]  
[b]Highlights:[/b]  

[b]Story:[/b] There isn’t one. You’re a goat. Make your own story. Maybe you’re a disgruntled farm animal on a quest for revenge. Or maybe you’re just vibing in a world where everything explodes when you touch it.  

[b]Graphics:[/b] Stunningly realistic… if the world was designed by someone who just discovered ragdoll physics and said, "[i]More. MORE![/i]"  

[b]Gameplay:[/b] Imagine playing Skyrim but with no quests, no objectives, and way more headbutting. It’s perfect for people who enjoy the feeling of total anarchy without consequences.  

[b]Soundtrack:[/b] Mostly goat bleats, explosions, and the sweet sound of destruction. It’s beautiful.  

[b]Replayability:[/b] Endless. Every time you boot it up, you’ll find a new, equally absurd way to destroy everything around you.  

[hr]  
[b]Pros:[/b]  
- You can become a demon goat, a robot goat, or even a goat that’s somehow a giraffe. Truly revolutionary character customization.  
- Break the laws of physics with zero remorse.  
- There’s a multiplayer mode, because why wreak havoc alone when you can bring friends?  

[b]Cons:[/b]  
- None. It’s a flawless work of art. (Okay, maybe it crashes sometimes, but let’s call that a feature.)  

[hr]  
[b]Final Thoughts:[/b]  

[b]Goat Simulator[/b] is not the game we deserve, but it’s the game we needed. It’s a love letter to chaos, and it reminds us all that sometimes, you just need to let loose and headbutt a car for no reason.  

[b]Rating:[/b] 10/10 – The [b]GOAT[/b] of all simulation games.

Goat Simulator is an absolutely bonkers game that embraces pure, unadulterated madness. If you're looking for a gaming experience that defies logic, revels in absurdity, and keeps you laughing until your sides hurt, then this game is an absolute must-play.

First things first, don't expect a deep storyline or complex objectives in Goat Simulator. Instead, prepare yourself for a hilarious sandbox filled with endless possibilities and a goat as your unconventional protagonist. From the moment you take control of your four-legged mayhem-maker, you're thrown into a world where physics take a backseat, and chaos reigns supreme.

The sheer amount of absurdity and comedic elements packed into Goat Simulator is mind-boggling. Whether you're licking objects to attach them to your goat tongue or launching yourself into the sky with the power of an explosive jetpack, every moment is a laugh-out-loud experience. The intentionally glitchy mechanics only add to the charm, resulting in unpredictable and downright hilarious situations at every turn.

Exploration is a key aspect of Goat Simulator, and the game's open-world environment is a playground of wacky surprises. From causing havoc in a quaint suburban neighborhood to wreaking havoc in a bustling city or even outer space, there's no shortage of bizarre scenarios to discover. The game encourages you to experiment, combining unlikely objects and interactions to create even more chaos.

The developers' commitment to embracing the absurd extends to the game's attention to detail. From the quirky physics engine to the intentionally humorous glitches, it's evident that Goat Simulator is a labor of love designed to tickle your funny bone. The game's tongue-in-cheek references to pop culture and gaming tropes add an extra layer of humor for those in the know.

While Goat Simulator may not be for everyone, it's a refreshing break from traditional gaming norms. It's a reminder that games can be purely fun and downright silly, providing an experience that is both entertaining and stress-relieving. So, if you're ready to let loose, embrace the madness, and embark on a hilarious adventure as a goat with no limits, Goat Simulator is waiting to whisk you away on a wild, unforgettable ride.

Simulation games haven't been a new concept for some time, and most of them take themselves extremely serious. They're one genre that gamers go to for solid immersion; Farming Simulator, Flight Simulator, Firefighter Simulator, the list carries on and on, especially when you get into the realm of VR. However, back in 2014 there was one game that wasn't having any of that immersion crap, and it proved to be one of the first comedy simulators to come about. By this point, some seven years later, Goat Simulator is pretty infamous, and rightfully so; it's full of bugs, glitches, and problems, but that's the very thing that makes it fun and entertaining. That's just the way it's supposed to be.

To clear up any possible confusion let's start by stating that Goat Simulator is a simulation game where you play as, well, a goat. There's no story or plot. There's no princess or maniacal villain. You can't even die, no matter how much you explode yourself, or how far you fall down, or even if your tongue gets stuck to a roller coaster that's going 100mph and it whips you around and flings you out into the abyss of the ocean. It's just you wreaking havoc in a small town as the world's most annoying goat. The base game comes with two maps, Goatville and Goat City Bay, the former of which is the small rural town with a construction site, gas station, car derby, and various houses to ransack, while the latter is a pier-area with a small funfair, some shops for the ramming, a sewer, and plenty of other areas to explore.

There's some inspiration taken from older Tony Hawk games, in that there are loads of special "challenges" to find and trigger. Everything from jumping over a soda can to finding a way to propel your goat-self so high up into the stratosphere that you reach actual space. There's also a certain Grand Theft Auto charm to it as well, probably due to the sheer absurdity of what can happen to your goat-self. There's a ton of stuff to do, and a lot of exploration to be had, though overall doing everything will only net you about 3-5 hours of playtime. The sandbox itself is small, but if you're the type who really enjoys seeing how much fun you can get out of ridiculous simulators, you can probably find a solid 8 hours of enjoyment out of Goat Simulator's base offering.

If you're looking for a way to kill a boring afternoon, or you need to add some humour to your day, Goat Simulator might just be the answer you're looking for. It's a fun little gem to come back to time and time again throughout the years, and it's regularly on sale for just a couple of bucks. The developers also expanded the base game with a few DLC packs, all of which are equally as fun and put your goat-self in other fun scenarios. Normally, a game of this calibre wouldn't make it as such a successful title, but Goat Simulator manages to be perfectly imperfect in all of the right ways.

Goat Simulator, I am confident that that name will be remembered by me, as one of the most revolutionary pieces of gaming, if not media in general. As of this review I have played this game for one hundred and six hours; to put that into perspective that would be 4.416667 days. In my humble opinion, to say that this game is "good" does not do it justice. I will explain my reasoning and logic as to why this is one of the greatest games of all time.

Paragraph one: The appearance.
When I say the appearance, I mean the marketing, the artwork, the community, and how it is perceived by the public. Let us start with the banner of this game, it simply says "Goat Simulator" with a picture of a goat to the right, there is a beautiful scenic background of a pasture, and the font choice mimics that of the popular "Simulator" genre. All of this fits well in a collage that perfectly encompasses the "Gist" of this game. It really is a Goat Simulator, tried and true, through and through. That is more than you can say for many other games indie games on the market today, it doesn't lie. This game is extremely genuine, for instance this game is not meant to be taken very seriously, it was released on April fools and for the amount of content in the game, it is priced relatively cheap. To me that screams "passion" Coffee Stain studios did not make this game (at least solely) for the monetary value, they made it because they wanted to, and in a world where triple A media dominates the videogaming market, made by big corporations that force microtransactions, and care more about the bottom line than artistic integrity, I think that this game is valuable. This game became popular when famous youtuber Markeplier played it, at face value the game seemed enjoyable, you could tell he was having legitimate fun, and not just putting on a show for the views. When that happened, people flocked to the game, and there was an increase in sales. But people did not value the game on the level of one of the beloved triple A titles, it was more of a silly little obscure one-off to them, a quick game-on-the-go if you will; and for that, people did not explore the detailed maps created by Coffee stain, and thus, much of the content was missed.

Paragraph two: The game.
When a player starts up the game for the very first time, they are greeted by the message "Press the "Any" key" some player might be dumbfounded for a mere millisecond, until they realize that the game just wants them to press a button. The wordage there shows that this game was not rushed, and it did not feel that it needed to be held to any standard other than what the creators intended, and let us face it, it was a funny joke. When you start up the title screen will play a scenic birds-eye tour of the town "Goatville" as you hear the games iconic and distinct music. When you load in, you are simply a goat, that's it, you are a goat in a petting zoo or something, you are given no direction, no tasks, you just started the game, and what you do next is completely up to you. This is not something seen in many other open-world games. For instance, in the Fallout franchise you are given an incentive to leave the comfort (or discomfort) of your spawn location, IE: "Find a water chip to fix your vaults plumbing!" or "Find your Father!" or "Find your son!" or "Find the Italian mobster that shot you in the head and only stole a poker chip for some reason!" in those scenarios you are given stimuli to explore, whereas here, exploration is an option, you could do frontflips off the local furniture, you could climb the goat tower, you could try to escape, the options are all yours. This is not to say that exploration is not rewarded, it totally is! By exploring the landscape you unlock Mutators (superpowers), you collect trophies, and not to mention the landscape itself. The simplicity of Goatville and Goat city bay makes them feel genuine and real, you may find a man in a tracksuit jogging along a dirt road in the countryside, or a group of protesters, or even the Devs themselves. The landscape is beautiful. Goatville takes place in a small, quiet, semi-rural settlement in the mid-morning, without giving too much information away, there are different areas that you can explore here, two woodland sections with occult secrets, an open field, a construction area, and a more developed region. It feels like a place you have been before, it feels up to scale, and real.

Paragraph three: The DLC.
This review is getting long-winded so I should probably make this short. The DLC offers more parody content, however instead of parodying the oh so popular "Simulator" genre, these parody the likes of Payday, Mass effect, World of Warcraft, and DayZ. These are much like the main game, and add their own mutators and achievements to the game, this spices things up. I personally really like the DLC, although it may not share as big of an effect as the main content, I think that it still deserves a similar amount of respect.

Paragraph four: The conclusion.
In short this game holds much more than it may seem, and I highly recommend that you play it in full, and download and play all of the DLC, if you really can't stand it, and prefer more serious and normal games, that's completely up to you, but this will always stand out as one of my favorite games of all time.

[b]Goat Simulator[/b] is pure, unfiltered nonsense — and that’s exactly the point. It throws logic off a cliff and replaces it with physics-breaking madness, ragdoll chaos, and a goat that headbutts cars into orbit. There’s no goal. No rules. Just destruction, glitches, and glorious absurdity.

🎮 Whether you’re bungee-jumping from helicopters, joining goat cults, licking people into traffic, or flying with a jetpack strapped to your back — the sandbox is your chaotic playground. It's intentionally buggy, gloriously unpredictable, and hilariously dumb in the best way possible.

🐐 The fun comes from discovery. You'll stumble into weird Easter eggs, broken events, and bizarre scenarios like goat zombies, demon rituals, and even parodies of other games. It’s like Grand Theft Auto if you replaced the gangsters with a deranged barnyard animal.

And with multiplayer and expansions, the mayhem only multiplies — goats in space? Goats as MMO characters? Yes, it’s real. And yes, it’s ridiculous.

🧨 Pure Sandbox Chaos — no limits, no logic, all fun.

🧪 Mod & Expansion Support — from space goats to goat-thulhu.

🔁 Shallow Gameplay — not much structure or long-term progression.

[/code]

[b]Goat Simulator[/b] is stupid. Broken. Pointless. And [b]completely brilliant in its stupidity[/b]. It's a meme turned into a game — and if you're down for some mindless, unforgettable laughs, this goat is ready to headbutt your boredom away.

Thoroughly enjoyed Goat Simulator 2014. Goat/10.
Goat Simulator 2014 gives an in-depth experience that uses a wide range of engaging stimulus and challenges to educate us humans of the agricultural environment that a goat must endure through it's life. The inspiring story of Goat overcoming his/her oppressors (the humans) creates an amazing storyline, with numerous plot twists that will have you on the edge of your seat. I know what you're thinking, "but its just a goat!" Shut the hell up you fool, although this may be 'just a goat', this is 'just a goat' that broke through its goat expectations and stereotypes to face the world with nothing but its hyper-elastic tongue and it's oddly unnatural ability to not die. Ever. Goat Simulator 2014 expertly demonstrates how political views and actions can affect not only mankind, but also goats. It confronts the player with many terrifying situations (and can at times cause great offense). One example of this is the many rules and regulations imposed by the goverment, like what the hell? You want to keep me in this goat pen? Do you think this tower will keep me happy? This game allows you to fight the power, and essentially "fuck the police". The most controversial aspect of this game is most definitely the goat fight scene, where you must turn against your fellow goats for the pleasure of the humans. Who really wants to participate in a competitive blood bath of goats for someone else's entertainment? In my honest opinion, I would much rather prefer that to not be a part of the game. Although I may not be condoning goat on goat violence, I find mowing down the many so called 'innocent' civilians and sacrificing them to the Lord Satan gives me an enjoyable rush. This game has the potential to inspire many, whether they want to become a goat scientist, goat gymnast, goat astronaut, goat ball pitcher or whale, they will find this game absolutely enthralling. The Good Goat VS Bad Goat dynamic of Goat Simulator gives the player the ability to influence the goat's decisions, and essentially determine to be Good Goat, or Bad Goat. (I also have the sneaking suspicions that recent games such as Infamous: SECOND SUN (what does that even mean?) have copied this genius game mechanic from Goat Simulator 2014.) 

 I recommend this game as it accurately depicts the various aspects of survival that a goat must face in it's day to life, and does so in a way that us humans can relate to and take advice from in both an entertaining and interesting way. This game forces you to think. I love it.

Goat Simulator began as a joke. This joke has now snowballed into what may be the greatest game of all time. Just when you think it can't get any weirder, this game will blow your mind. It has references to nearly every geeky thing you can think of, from The IT Crowd to South Park to Bravest Warriors.

A lot of games out there have stupid achievements. As a completionist, I feel compelled to 100% each game in my collection even though it kills me a little inside. With Goat Simulator, you can breeze through all the achievements in a few hours if that's what you want - the mutations make it super easy. But I didn't take the easy route. For all its frustrating bits, I wanted to do everything this game has to offer, and I wanted to do it legit. Aside from a few gems like Super Meat Boy and VVVVVV, not many games can do that.

If you want hours upon hours of replayable, sandboxy goodness with the option of getting serious now and then, Goat Simulator is for you.
